name: Xona XC-SF150-X4 in Ramona Chip Holder 4 well
author: Ramona Optics
part_number: XC-SF150-X4 in Ramona Xona X4 chip holder
notes:
The four wells of this definition are the four chips' imaging regions, one well per chip, each spanning that chip's four microgroove barriers A-D. It is the file to select when four Xona XC-SF150-X4 chips are loaded in the Ramona holder. 

WHY ONE WELL PER CHIP AND NOT SIXTEEN - the request asked to be told which was chosen. Sixteen imaging regions sit on a 12.00mm row pitch (the four units A-D within a chip) and a 27.00mm column pitch (chip to chip). The schema has a single 'pitch' shared by rows and columns (labware/schema.py, WellDimensions.pitch), so a 12 x 27mm lattice cannot be written, and the request's own fallback is taken: 1 row x 4 columns on the 27.00mm column pitch, with each well a rectangle that spans all four barriers of one chip. The consequence a user sees is that the plate has four addressable wells, A1-A4, one per chip, rather than sixteen; each well's scan covers that chip's four imaging regions and the 11.00mm gaps between them. 

GEOMETRY. From the request and confirmed against the chip drawing: in the holder the chips lie with their 75.50mm axis along the plate's 85.48mm width, so the four units of a chip step in y and the chips step in x. The unit centres are at y = 24.74, 36.74, 48.74 and 60.74mm - A at 42.74 - 3 x 12.00 / 2 = 24.74 - and the chip columns at the pocket centres x = 23.38, 50.38, 77.38 and 104.38mm. Each well is therefore 4.00mm across the barriers (x, the plate's length) by 3 x 12.00 + 1.00 = 37.00mm along the chip (y, the plate's width), centred at y = 42.74mm, spanning y 24.24-61.24mm, well inside the pocket's 4.99-80.49mm. 'diameter' repeats the shorter side, 4.00mm. 

THE HOLDER. NOT A CATALOGUE PLATE. This is a Ramona Optics fixture: an SBS-footprint holder that carries four Xona XonaChip X4 chips (75.50 x 25.50mm, slide format) so that they can be driven as one plate. Xona themselves describe the arrangement - 'these chips (the size of standard microscope slides) can be combined in a 4-slide plate holder to yield sixteen (16) sample units' - but the holder in this file is Ramona's, not Xona's, and no drawing of it exists yet; the #team_vireo thread the request cites discusses making 'a stand-in stand that we make here'. 

REQUESTED, and therefore exact by definition rather than sourced: the 127.76 x 85.48mm ANSI/SLAS footprint with a standard skirt; four rectangular pockets of 25.50 x 75.50mm plus a small clearance, long axis along the plate's width; pocket centres 27mm apart in x at 23.38, 50.38, 77.38 and 104.38mm, which is three times the MCAM's 9mm micro-camera pitch so every chip sits under the same camera column; and the pocket centre line at y = 42.74mm. Those four x values are symmetric about 63.88mm = 127.76 / 2 and 42.74 = 85.48 / 2, so the block of pockets is centred on the plate, as the request says. GEOMETRY CHECK: the pockets span x 10.63-36.13, 37.63-63.13, 64.63-90.13 and 91.63-117.13mm, leaving a 1.50mm rib between neighbouring pockets and 10.63mm of plate at each end, and y 4.99-80.49mm, leaving 4.99mm at each side. Nothing overruns the footprint. 

POCKET CLEARANCE: the request says '25.50 x 75.50 mm plus a small clearance' and does not give the clearance, so the pockets are recorded at the chip's nominal 25.50 x 75.50mm and the clearance is left out rather than invented. A machined holder will be slightly larger; the chip can then sit off centre in its pocket by half the clearance, which is the dominant positioning error of this fixture and is NOT captured by any field in this file. 

NOT SPECIFIED BY ANYONE, recorded here as provisional values that must be replaced from the holder's drawing before it is made, and listed as open questions on the request issue: (a) outer_plate_dimensions.height 14.35mm is the ANSI/SLAS 2-2004 microplate height, used because the request says only 'SBS-footprint ... with standard skirt'; (b) the pocket depth, recorded as 1.0mm so that a chip of the inferred 1.0mm thickness sits flush with the holder's top face - it is a consequence of the chip thickness, which Xona does not publish either; (c) the holder's material and colour, left out entirely (no bottom_material, wall_material, bottom_color or wall_color), since the holder may be machined aluminium, 3D printed plastic or acrylic and that decides whether it can be imaged through at all; (d) whether each pocket is a blind pocket or a through-hole, which decides whether the chips can be used on a transmitted-light instrument. The skirt keys are left at the schema's documented defaults, which are the ANSI/SLAS standard skirt the request asked for.

THE CHIP. CONTROLLING DOCUMENTS, both published by Xona Microfluidics on their XC-SF150-X4 product page. (1) The dimensioned plan drawing 'XC-SF150-x4-InnerDim.png' (drawing_reference), which prints, as callouts: 75.50mm overall length, 25.50mm overall width, 19.75mm from the end of the chip to the centre line of unit A, 12.00mm unit-to-unit pitch, 10.00mm between the centres of the two large wells of a unit, 7.00mm between the centres of the two small ports of a unit, O6.0 for the large wells and O2.0 for the small ports. A companion drawing 'XC-SF150-x4-OuterDim.png' repeats 75.50 x 25.50mm, and 'XC-SF150-x4-UnitView.png' is an undimensioned enlarged plan of one unit. The drawings carry no revision or date; they were uploaded in 2023-02 per their URL. (2) The vendor's specification text, spread over the product page, the XONACHIPS page, the FAQ page and the 'Introducing XonaChips' / 'Introducing the X4 XonaChip' posts: '(4) compartmentalized culture units, each with 150 um wide microgroove barriers'; 'Each unit contains (18) microgrooves connecting the compartments'; 'Each microgroove cross-section for all XonaChips is approximately 7 um x 7 um'; 'Main channel heights are approximately 80 um'; 'a smaller cell loading port approximately 2 mm in diameter'; 'XonaChips are made of cyclic olefin copolymer (COC)'; 'The XonaChip consists of a molded COC top bonded to a thin optically transparent 150 um thick COC film'; 'The outside dimensions of the X4 chip are the same as a standard microscope slide'; 'Size: 75 mm x 25 mm'. Where the catalogue text's rounded '75 mm x 25 mm' and the drawing's 75.50 x 25.50mm disagree, the drawing is followed. 

MATERIAL, answering the request's question directly: this chip is NOT PDMS on a glass coverslip. Xona's FAQ separates the two product lines - 'The silicone devices are made of poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) and XonaChips are made of cyclic olefin copolymer (COC)'. XC-SF150-X4 is a XonaChip, an injection-moulded COC top bonded to a 150 um COC film, so bottom_material and wall_material are cyclo_olefin and bottom_thickness is the published 150 um film. The PDMS part with the same barrier is the separate SF150x2 'Small Footprint Silicone Device', which is a different part and a different size (about 28 x 18 mm). No refractive index is published for the film and none is recorded; COC is typically about 1.53 at 589 nm, which is NOT taken from a Xona document and is mentioned here for orientation only. 

THE IMAGING REGION, and how its size was obtained. The request asks for a well that covers the microgroove barrier between the two compartment channels at the centre of a unit, sized from Xona's published specs. Xona publishes the barrier length (150 um) but publishes NO channel width and NO channel length for the X4 unit. The '1.5 mm x 7 mm x 0.060 mm (W x L x H) main channels' and '0.01 mm x 0.005 mm microgrooves' figures that circulate for XonaChips come from the JoVE protocol 'Use of Pre-Assembled Plastic Microfluidic Chips for Compartmentalizing Primary Murine Neurons' (doi:10.3791/58421), which describes the 2-compartment XC150 / XC450 / XC900 chips, not this small-footprint 4-unit chip, and they also contradict Xona's own site (80 um channel height, 7 x 7 um microgrooves). They were therefore NOT used. 
The region's size across the barrier is DERIVED from two printed callouts only: the two large wells of a unit are 10.00mm apart and are O6.0, so the open fluidic region between their edges is 10.00 - 6.00 = 4.00mm, centred on the unit's centre. The region's size along the channels is SCALED off the published UnitView drawing, assumed to scale: at 1600 x 1280 px the two O6.0 circles measure 420 px across and their centres 707 px apart, giving 70.0 px/mm and 70.7 px/mm in x, and the two O2.0 port centres measure 494 px apart, giving 70.6 px/mm in y - two independent calibrations per axis agreeing to 1% and the two axes agreeing to 0.2%. On that scale the microgroove bank, drawn as the hatched strip at the unit's centre, spans 71 px = 1.00mm, and the channel neck either side of it spans 71-80 px = 1.00-1.13mm. The well is therefore recorded as 4.00mm across the barrier by 1.00mm along the channels, centred on the unit's centre. Uncertainty on the 1.00mm value is about +/-0.1mm: the drawing's line weight is 4 px (0.06mm) and the two measurements of the neck differ by 0.13mm. It is corroborated by the vendor's own text: 18 microgrooves of 7 um width spread over 1.00mm is a 56 um groove pitch, which matches the drawn hatching. The 150 um barrier itself measures 15 px = 0.21mm on the same calibration, which is the printed 150 um plus two line widths, so the drawing is consistent with its own callout. 

NOT PUBLISHED BY XONA, and therefore not written as a vendor number anywhere in this file: overall chip thickness; well and port depths; reservoir working volumes; any tolerance; the chip's corner radius; sterility; surface treatment of the channels (the chips ship with a separate 'XC Pre-Coat' tube, which is a reagent, not a moulded-in treatment).

Z, and what is not recorded. bottom_thickness 150 um is the chip's COC film, the layer the objective looks through. bottom_elevation and floor_height are NOT recorded: they would be the pocket floor's height above the holder's resting plane plus the film, and the holder's section does not exist yet. 'depth' 80 um is the chip's published channel height, as in the chip-only file. Use 'pitch' and origin reference to compute all well centers.
